name: Place Pulse 1.0: Safety, Class and Uniqueness (4 cities)
description:
Method replication: same questions and pairwise design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (new Google Street View views of the same four cities, © Google). Salesses, Schechtner & Hidalgo (2013, PLoS ONE 8(7):e68400) built the original Place Pulse website: volunteers compared pairs of geo-tagged street images from Boston, New York, Linz and Salzburg on which looked safer, more upper-class and more unique. Images were scored with Q-scores. Perceptions of New York and Boston images spread more widely than those of Linz and Salzburg, which the authors read as more contrasting, unequal cityscapes; in New York, perceived safety and class correlated with homicides by zip code after controlling for income, population, area and age.

What participants do: after consent, 10 pairs each on "Which place looks safer?", "Which place looks more upper-class?" and "Which place looks more unique?", with an Equal option. Images come at random from 130 views: Boston 65, New York 29, Linz 19, Salzburg 17. Then age, gender and home city.

Analysis as in the paper: Q-score per image (win and loss rates corrected for opponents), then the spread of scores within each city to compare inequality of perception.

Differences from the original study: (1) the images are new Google Street View views (2016–2026) from random points in each city, not the paper's set; the four cities are not equally represented; (2) the original site allowed unlimited votes; this template asks 10 pairs per question. The earlier version of this template showed 7 photographs cropped from the paper PDF.
